agree.reason: The quarterly targets, the openly stated $32,000 gap and the June checkpoint would reassure most board members, but the two sales-minded members will ask why ads must stop in January rather than taper off, and the memo does not answer that.

honest.reason: It frames full replacement as a goal rather than a promise, which is careful, but it says ad revenue fell 'over two years' when the 36% drop happened in a single year, and its $67,000 projection for 2027 rests on that wrong pace.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out $96 per member, 875 members, 6.25% of the list and the $52,000 transition-year revenue, but it describes the target as 'four times the pilot' when the pilot pace of about 35 sign-ups a week is double the roughly 17 a week the target needs, so it misses the most favourable true framing.

right_comparison.reason: The memo does include a no-change scenario, but because it spreads a one-year 36% drop across two years it predicts $67,000 of ad revenue in 2027 instead of about $54,000, which makes the status quo look stronger than the facts show.

qualification.reason: Quarterly net-member targets with a 550-member check on June 30 give the board dates and numbers to verify, though the only consequence of missing the check is 'I will bring the board options.'

objections.reason: It deals with the transition gap and mentions the 11-year ad colleague, but the staff plan is left as a placeholder, it does not explain why a phased exit is ruled out, and it says nothing about how many members might cancel.

fit.reason: It is set out as a clear board memo and is roughly one page, though the risks section and the decision list push it to the limit.
